item.title: Costa Rica construye megacárcel inspirada en las prisiones de Bukele en El Salvador
item.description: Costa Rica inaugurará una nueva prisión de máxima seguridad con capacidad para más de 5.000 reclusos. El centro contará con celdas con rejas y camas de hormigón, bajo condiciones de vida austeras. Los internos solo tendrán derecho a una hora diaria al aire libre, una medida defendida por la presidenta costarricense, Laura Fernández. La prisión está inspirada en el modelo de alta seguridad impulsado por el presidente salvadoreño, Nayib Bukele. No obstante, organizaciones no gubernamentales han denunciado presuntas violaciones de derechos humanos, detenciones arbitrarias y cientos de muertes… Publicado también por: La Nación - El Mundo. item.title: Scorecard: Colombia gets top marks while high-emitting countries doing too little to protect health from climate change
item.description: The latest Healthy NDC Scorecard, published by the Global Climate and Health Alliance, finds that, Colombia integrates health most deeply into its national climate plan, closely followed by Nigeria and Cambodia. Conversely, the climate commitments of the governments of Japan, New Zealand and India fail to adequately consider health, while high-emitting economies, including EU members, China, Brazil and the U.K., refer to health in their national climate plans but do not match this with the ambitious emissions reduction targets required to protect health. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Brazil plants 840,000 trees to restore 607 hectares of Atlantic Forest
item.description: Brazil's Atlantic Forest is undergoing remarkable restoration efforts, spearheaded by World Land Trust and Reserva Ecológica de Guapiaçu. With 840,000 trees planted over 20 years, 607 hectares of degraded land have been revived into verdant forest. This initiative has created a vital wildlife corridor, facilitating the return of over 220 bird species to the previous wetland, while striving to protect and enhance the Guapiaçu watershed's remaining forest. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

The Observers team spoke to its founder, Rodney Jean Marc, who said their doors are open to everyone, “even children in armed gangs”. The initiative takes place as the country's security situation has worsened in recent years. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Pakistan ranks lowest in South Asia on hunger index amid rising food prices
item.description: Pakistan's 2026 Global Hunger Index standings reveal an alarming crisis, showcasing the worst performance in South Asia amid ongoing economic challenges. Soaring food prices and the increasing frequency of climate-related disasters have sharply intensified food insecurity. With around 218 million individuals in South Asia experiencing undernourishment from 2023 to 2025, urgent strategies are required to bolster access to healthy food and enhance agricultural resilience against severe weather patterns. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: América Latina exporta un 20 % más, con Asia ganando peso como socio
item.description: "La geografía comercial está cambiando", advierte la ONU. Las exportaciones de bienes de América Latina y el Caribe crecerán un 20 % en 2026, el mayor aumento desde 2021, impulsadas por los precios de los productos básicos en América del Sur y las manufacturas en México. Pero la región solo representa el 2 % del comercio mundial de servicios modernos, el segmento más dinámico. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: A fungus is threatening the world’s food supply. Scientists just found a new defense
item.description: Scientists have discovered a potential new weapon against a devastating fungus that threatens rice, wheat, and barley worldwide. By engineering a special type of plant immune receptor, researchers created defenses capable of recognizing multiple fungal threats at once. The breakthrough could eventually lead to crops with powerful, long-lasting disease resistance, helping protect a global food supply increasingly threatened by spreading infections and climate change. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
